question: A 15-year-old boy presents to the emergency department after a rusty nail pierced through his right foot. He was able to pull out the nail, but not able to walk on his foot. He believes he had all his shots as a child, with the last one just before starting middle school at the age of 12. The vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination reveals a 0.5-inch puncture wound on the right heel. The site is tender, erythematous, with flecks of reddish-brown particles in the base. No blood or discharge is seen. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.opa: Clean and dress the wound only
options.opc: Administer Tdap, Td, and TIG (tetanus immune globulin)

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "15-year-old boy with puncture wound" -> "rusty nail injury" -> "risk of tetanus infection" -> "last tetanus shot at age 12" -> "consider need for booster" -> "Tdap or Td recommended" -> "administer Td and TIG" -> 85%

CHAIN: "15-year-old boy with puncture wound" -> "rusty nail injury" -> "potential for tetanus exposure" -> "last vaccination at age 12" -> "unclear if fully immunized" -> "administer Tdap, Td, and TIG" -> 75%
CHAIN: "15-year-old boy with puncture wound" -> "rusty nail injury" -> "risk of tetanus" -> "last shot at age 12" -> "Tdap recommended for adolescents" -> "administer Tdap only" -> 70%

CHAIN: "15-year-old boy with puncture wound" -> "rusty nail injury" -> "risk of tetanus" -> "last vaccination at age 12" -> "Td and TIG indicated for high-risk injury" -> "administer Td and TIG" -> 90%
analysis: The patient is a 15-year-old boy who has a puncture wound from a rusty nail. Given that he received his last tetanus vaccination at age 12, he is likely due for a booster. The presence of a puncture wound, especially from a rusty object, raises the concern for tetanus. The standard recommendation is to administer Td (tetanus-diphtheria) if the last booster was more than 5 years ago for dirty wounds. Since he is 15 and had his last shot at 12, he is due for Td. However, since the wound is dirty (rusty nail), it is also prudent to administer Tetanus Immune Globulin (TIG) if the patient's vaccination history is uncertain or if it has been more than 5 years since the last Td. Therefore, the most appropriate next step in management is to administer Td and TIG.
